clue.text: Failure of play to work on the queen

parts.note: Noh is the classical Japanese drama
OP is short for opus, a work
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A theatre production flops because it relies on the monarch's patronage.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone or something with no chance of success, a failure in the making.

clue.text: More than one song

definitions.meaning: 'a ... of' things means several, more than one
a song in a performance or on a record

explanation.surface: Several songs, as in a medley.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'a number of people' the word means several; a musical piece in a show is also called this.

clue.text: Workers getting depressed easily

parts.note: hands are labourers, workers
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Employees become dispirited with no effort at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning by this margin is an idiom for doing it with ease, comfortably.

clue.text: Add to strike

definitions.meaning: to ... weight or speed is to add to it
to strike an attitude or pose is to adopt it, to put it on for show

explanation.surface: Something increasing the pressure of an industrial walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to increase (put on pounds) and to assume a pose or manner.

clue.text: Copy of Rushdie's first epic tale destroyed

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of Rushdie's name only
destroyed says the letters of epic tale are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A duplicate of an early Rushdie novel has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges EPICTALE into EPLICATE, after R from 'Rushdie's first'.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to make an exact duplicate, to reproduce something.

clue.text: Reserved when first introduced to lawyer by conservationists

indicators.note: introduced to says the next piece is put inside the lawyer's abbreviation

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor
1ST, with the figure one read as letter I
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: A shy person, meeting a lawyer from an environmental group for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word. The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is cool and aloof, keeping others at a distance.

clue.text: Note to Rob is amusing

parts.note: D is a musical note
to roll someone is slang for to rob them

explanation.surface: A message telling Rob he is funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Droll describes humour that is dry and quaintly funny.

clue.text: Trace it back to the source of nutrients in a plant

indicators.note: in says the pieces before it go inside the plant's name

parts.note: Scilla is the squill, a bulb plant of the lily family

indicators.note: the source of picks the opening letter of nutrients
back says the word it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Instructions to trace the nutrient supply of a plant to its origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trace' looks like an instruction but is the definition; the plant is the squill, a garden bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: A scintilla is a tiny amount, a mere trace or spark of something.

clue.text: Extremely rare to fill an American sports stadium

indicators.note: to fill says the pick from rare goes inside the other pieces
Extremely picks the letters at the two ends of rare

explanation.surface: Seldom does a crowd pack out a US sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: RE goes after the first A of ANA.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sports and spectacles.

clue.text: Row over race causing a suppressed snigger

indicators.note: over says the row piece covers, enclosing, the race piece

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An argument about race prompts a stifled laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but it means a line of seats. The TT is the famous Isle of Man motorbike race.
explanation.definitionFit: A titter is a short, half-stifled giggle.

clue.text: A passage from Rosenblum on Etty as a painter

indicators.note: A passage from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An excerpt from an art critic's essay about William Etty as a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Rosenblum was an art historian and William Etty an English painter, so the surface stays in the gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter, an example of the category.

clue.text: Prudent to conceal identity in test on books

indicators.note: to conceal says the test word wraps around the identity abbreviation

parts.note: to prove is to test, as in a proving ground
ID is short for identity
NT is the New Testament, its books

explanation.surface: It is wise to hide who you are when examined on books.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means careful to provide for the future, thrifty and prudent.

clue.text: It's absolutely necessary when lease isn't renewed

indicators.note: renewed says the letters of lease isn't are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: A tenant insisting a lease must be renewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'renewed' looks like the tenancy's fate but it rearranges LEASEISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is indispensable, needed without question.

clue.text: Josh drinks last of coke

parts.note: teas are drinks

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of coke

explanation.surface: Someone called Josh downs the dregs of a cola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Josh' reads as a name but it is the verb to josh, meaning to rib.
explanation.definitionFit: To josh someone is to tease them good-humouredly.

clue.text: Pen company starts to offer pensions

indicators.note: starts to picks the opening letters of offer and pensions

explanation.surface: A writing-pen firm begins offering pension schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is an enclosure for poultry, and a pen is an animal enclosure.

clue.text: Fellow maintaining essential bit of wiring on container ship

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the fellow word keeps the rest inside it

parts.note: a peer is an equal, a fellow

indicators.note: essential bit of picks the central letters of wiring

parts.note: a vat is a large container for liquids

explanation.surface: A chap keeps the vital wiring of a container vessel in order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container ship' reads as one phrase, but 'container' is wordplay and 'ship' alone defines; 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was a privately owned armed vessel licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Pass over after everyone gets permission to proceed

indicators.note: after says the pass-over piece is placed following the everyone piece

parts.note: all means everyone
to clear a hurdle is to pass over it

explanation.surface: Once a pass has been granted to everyone, they may go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the signal that danger is past and one may proceed.

clue.text: Incomplete details initially emerging after battle ceases

indicators.note: after says the emerging letter follows the battle name

parts.note: Loos was a First World War battle in 1915

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of emerging

parts.note: ends means stops, ceases

explanation.surface: Leftover matters start to surface once the fighting stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are unfinished matters, details still to be tied up.

clue.text: Conformity shown by unruly teenager in minutes? Just the opposite

indicators.note: in, reversed by the closing instruction, means the minutes letter goes inside the scrambled teenager
Just the opposite flips the containment, so the teenager surrounds the minutes rather than sitting inside
unruly says the letters of teenager run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A wild adolescent shows up in the meeting record, which seems unlikely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' turns TEENAGER into AGREEENT; 'Just the opposite' reverses 'in', so M goes inside it rather than the teenager going inside minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreement means accord or correspondence, conformity with something.

clue.text: Hamlet, for example, is another one in torment

indicators.note: in torment says the letters writhe and are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The Danish prince is yet another tortured soul.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a protagonist lacking conventional heroic qualities, an example of the type.

clue.text: A measure of port

definitions.meaning: a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards
A historic port city in northern Israel

explanation.surface: A tot of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink; it is the harbour city of Acre in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a unit of area and an ancient Levantine harbour town.

clue.text: Guard meets resistance from swordsman

parts.note: a fence is a barrier that guards
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A sentry is up against opposition from a swordsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A fencer is someone who fights with a sword in the sport of fencing.

clue.text: Left inside badly finished work causing an irregular discoloration

indicators.note: inside says the left letter sits within the work word

parts.note: a botch is a job done badly

explanation.surface: A shoddy job leaves an uneven stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch is a patch of uneven colour on skin or a surface.

clue.text: More evident in complex tracery

indicators.note: evident in says the letters can be seen inside the words complex tracery

explanation.surface: Further detail shows up in intricate stonework patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than usual.

clue.text: Wrong about including university swimmer

indicators.note: including says the reversed word takes the university letter inside
about says the word for a wrong is turned round

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A mistaken story about a college swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses TORT to TROT, then 'including' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, and a fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: It's intended to be eaten by man bit by bit

parts.note: a man in chess or draughts is a piece
a meal is food meant to be eaten

explanation.surface: Something meant to be consumed slowly by a person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Piecemeal means done gradually, in stages rather than all at once.

clue.text: Poke around top of ugly swelling

indicators.note: around says the poke word goes round the letter from ugly

parts.note: to prod is to poke

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of ugly in this down clue

explanation.surface: Prodding at the head of a nasty lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud describes something raised above a surface, as with proud flesh, so swelling.

clue.text: Present tenant's heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the tenant word is removed

parts.note: a renter is a tenant; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A tenant who is here now is on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the R from RENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter evidence or a plea is to present it formally.

clue.text: Fold near to the bottom

parts.note: close means near
down means towards the bottom

explanation.surface: Folding something close to its lower edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fold' is not creasing paper but a business failing.
explanation.definitionFit: When a business folds it ceases trading, it shuts for good.

clue.text: Discuss Handel on the radio

definitions.meaning: to ... a topic is to deal with it in speech or writing
the composer's name said on air is 'handle', and to handle something is to deal with it

explanation.surface: Talking about a Handel broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part works in two steps: Handel heard sounds like handle, which means treat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean to deal with: treating a subject in a lecture and handling something.

clue.text: Withdrew from ceremony over occupying soldiers beginning to desert

indicators.note: occupying says the turned ceremony word sits inside the soldiers abbreviation

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

indicators.note: over says the ceremony word is turned round

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of desert

explanation.surface: Pulling out of a parade as troops started to abandon their posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Engineers are a British army corps, a common source of the soldiers abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired means went away, withdrew, as to retire from a room.

clue.text: Animal crackers primarily available in school to make money

indicators.note: in says the animal and its partner go inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: a rat is an animal

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of crackers

explanation.surface: Animal-shaped biscuits on sale at school as a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal crackers' looks like the biscuit; 'available' and 'to make' are link words. RATC goes after SC.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch is slang for money, cash.
